stages.name: Requirements
stages.entryQuestion: Before designing a distributed rate limiter, what scope and scale assumptions would you clarify?
stages.objective: Agree on product behavior, measurable quality targets and the stated exercise workload.

completionCriteria.name: Functional scope
completionCriteria.guidance: Define who is limited, which routes share a budget, what a burst means, and the scope of a policy change.

completionCriteria.name: Quality targets
completionCriteria.guidance: Separate decision latency from protected API latency; decide fail-open or fail-closed per endpoint and explain quota accuracy.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity estimates
completionCriteria.guidance: Use the fictional baseline or state a justified alternative; derive average and peak rates and distinguish payload bytes from replication and indexes.

stages.name: High Level Design
stages.entryQuestion: Where does the limiter sit, and what state is on the request path?
stages.objective: Separate synchronous budget checks from policy distribution and observability.

completionCriteria.name: Enforcement boundary
completionCriteria.guidance: Place enforcement at a gateway, service library or dedicated service with authenticated tenant identity.

completionCriteria.name: Policy path
completionCriteria.guidance: Cache versioned policies near enforcement while keeping a durable control-plane source.

completionCriteria.name: Budget state
completionCriteria.guidance: Route the same tenant-user-route key to one atomic state owner or a coordinated equivalent.

stages.name: Core Flow
stages.entryQuestion: Walk through a burst and two simultaneous requests against your chosen algorithm.
stages.objective: Specify a correct budget transition rather than listing algorithm names.

completionCriteria.name: Algorithm semantics
completionCriteria.guidance: Choose token bucket, sliding-window counter/log or another suitable method; explain its actual burst behavior.

completionCriteria.name: Atomic transition
completionCriteria.guidance: Compute refill, decision and deduction in one atomic operation or CAS retry loop; avoid a separate read and write race.

completionCriteria.name: Time and retry delay
completionCriteria.guidance: Use a stable time source and nonnegative elapsed time; derive Retry-After from the next permissible request rather than guessing.

completionCriteria.name: Bounded state
completionCriteria.guidance: Expire idle buckets safely so expiry cannot create extra budget earlier than a full refill would.

stages.name: Data Model
stages.entryQuestion: What bucket keys and fields do you store, and how do policy changes affect them?
stages.objective: Model budget state and versioned policy with bounded cardinality.

completionCriteria.name: Key isolation
completionCriteria.guidance: Include tenant, principal and route/policy scope; use authenticated identifiers and bound attacker-controlled cardinality.

completionCriteria.name: Bucket schema
completionCriteria.guidance: For a token bucket, store tokens, last refill time and policy version; use the equivalent state for another chosen algorithm.

completionCriteria.name: Policy migration
completionCriteria.guidance: Define how new limits affect existing balances and remove obsolete buckets without granting repeated fresh bursts.

stages.name: Reliability
stages.entryQuestion: What should the API do if the state store times out or a replica is behind?
stages.objective: Make quota accuracy and outage behavior explicit.

completionCriteria.name: Outage policy
completionCriteria.guidance: Choose fail-open or fail-closed by endpoint risk; distinguish a store error from a true rate-limit denial.

completionCriteria.name: State consistency
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain how replicas, failover or retries can overspend a quota and bound or prevent that error.

completionCriteria.name: Recovery safety
completionCriteria.guidance: Handle time skew, stale policy caches and reconnect bursts without negative token balances.

stages.name: Scaling
stages.entryQuestion: How would you handle 300000 peak checks/s and one disproportionately hot tenant?
stages.objective: Scale across keys while recognizing single-key serialization limits.

completionCriteria.name: Shard ownership
completionCriteria.guidance: Partition by a stable bucket key, with explicit shard movement and regional ownership.

completionCriteria.name: Hot keys
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain why more shards do not split one strictly atomic hot bucket; use local allocations or hierarchical quotas only with an error budget.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity budget
completionCriteria.guidance: Estimate 1.6 GB of logical state for 20 million 80-byte buckets, then add keys, allocator overhead, replicas and peak CPU/network cost.

stages.name: Tradeoffs
stages.entryQuestion: How would you trade quota precision, latency and global availability?
stages.objective: Defend an algorithm and regional coordination policy.

completionCriteria.name: Algorithm tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare the selected algorithm with a fixed or sliding-window alternative; describe boundary bursts and memory cost.

completionCriteria.name: Regional tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare a globally coordinated budget with partitioned regional allowances and document possible overshoot.

completionCriteria.name: Operational tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Measure allowed/denied/error decisions, decision latency and hot-key saturation without using raw principal IDs as labels.
